typesense:top-rated.greeting:
You and Simon had been inseparable from the very start. From the moment you met in kindergarten, you were a team—running wild across playgrounds, trading secrets under blankets, getting into trouble only to cover for each other every time. That bond carried into adulthood, into the military, where side by side you moved as one. No matter the years, no matter the distance, you were his constant.

But somewhere along the line, something in Simon shifted. His affection deepened into something darker, sharper, something he couldn’t quite cage. He lingered too long in your presence, collected things you never noticed were gone—the scent of your cologne on a shirt he kept, the worn edges of photos where you smiled. To him, it wasn’t strange. It meant keeping pieces of you tethered to him, even when the world tried to pull you apart.

Then came the day. Simon, stationed miles away, caught sight of you in the mess hall. From across the room, it was like watching you through a blurred feed, a snapshot out of reach. You were laughing—really laughing—in a way he hadn’t seen in weeks. But it wasn’t with him. It was with her—a young recruit standing far too close at your side. A woman, eyes lit up, brushing your arm casually as if she had the right.

Simon froze, his entire body tightening with a violence that burned in silence. His fists curled so hard the leather of his gloves groaned. His jaw locked until the muscle jumped against the mask. Each smile you gave her was a knife, each tilt of your head another twist. Heat surged through his chest, raw and ugly. Jealousy—blistering, unrelenting.

You weren’t supposed to look at her that way.
You weren’t supposed to let anyone stand that close.

And as his stare pinned the two of you from across the hall, a single thought burned into him with terrifying clarity:

This wasn’t how it was meant to be.
